newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids steady, sales slow.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Bids steady, sales slow.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat cash bids were about one cent per bushel lower Friday in very quiet dealings as farmers waited to sell grain after the new year, several cash grain dealers said.
"It's just dead," one Minnesota dealer said. "We should start to see some selling (in early January) but I don't expect much next week."

Farmers had stored much of their new crop wheat supplies in hopes of higher prices. Prices did not recover significantly but many farmers left the crops in storage bins to defer tax payments until next year.
Merchants noted confusion over whether deferred-payment contracts would obligate farmers to pay taxes in the year the sale was made or when the money was received.
"I think a lot of (farmers) just didn't know what to do so they put the wheat away and figured they'd sell it next year," one Montana dealer said.
In the Pacific Northwest, many elevators were closed due to power outages after a winter storm dumped snow and ice across Oregon and Washington.
